absent: Auxiliary clock enable and disable implementation behind the sysfs store path.
Timekeeper shadow update and clock validation handling outside the shown tail.
Full timer queue insertion and deletion and next expiry recalculation.
Tickless next event computation and remote migration handling.
Debug file operations backing the sleep time display.
Complete sysctl registration lifetime and failure handling.
Jiffies increment path and tick interrupt handling.
Lockdep and debug object framework semantics.

findings.text: The timer wheel advances levels in units of three bits, giving a divisor of eight and a low mask of seven used to decide whether a higher level must be examined.
Each wheel level encodes six bits, giving sixty four vectors per level with an intra level mask of sixty three.

Wheel depth has two build variants of nine and eight levels. The far timeout cutoff is the start index of the deepest level, the maximum wheel timeout is that cutoff minus one granule of the last level, total vectors equal per level size times depth, and level granularity grows as a power of two of the level shift.
Timer bases have two build variants. One provides three bases with local zero and global one and default two. The other provides a single base where local and global and default all collapse to zero.
Timer modification option values are one for pending only and two for reduce and four for not pending.
Clocksource name storage allows thirty two characters and the sleep duration histogram uses thirty two bins.

Per CPU timer base storage timer_bases holds lock and running_timer and clk and next_expiry and cpu and next_expiry_recalc and is_idle and timers_pending and pending_map and vectors, with one bitmap bit per wheel vector and one hash list per vector, plus expiry_lock and timer_waiters on real time builds.

Rounding services round_jiffies and round_jiffies_relative and round_jiffies_up and round_jiffies_up_relative plus __round_jiffies_relative and __round_jiffies_up_relative cover absolute and relative values with normal and upward only forms and explicit CPU or current CPU variants.

Rounding skews the target by three jiffies per CPU number, then rounds to whole second boundaries with a quarter second threshold for choosing down versus up unless upward rounding is forced, removes the skew, and keeps the original value when the rounded value is no longer in the future.

Timer arming services mod_timer and mod_timer_pending and timer_reduce and add_timer_global allow modifying expiry unconditionally and only when already pending and shortening only, plus adding to the global base after clearing the pinned attribute and warning when already pending.

Timer lifetime services timer_init_key and timer_init_key_on_stack and timer_shutdown and timer_shutdown_sync and timer_delete_sync_try provide normal and stack initialization with callback and flags and lockdep identity, plus shutdown and synchronous shutdown and a non blocking synchronous delete attempt.

Initialization detaches queue linkage and records the callback, masks unsupported flag bits while recording the current CPU number, establishes lockdep identity, and performs debug object initialization with tracing, using an on stack variant for stack resident timers.

Timer debug objects identify static objects by empty linkage with a static marker, resolve delayed_work_timer_fn and kthread_delayed_work_timer_fn through an offset table to the underlying work function, and repair misuse by deleting and reinitializing active timers on init and installing a warning stub when activation precedes init and warning on double activation and deleting plus freeing active timers on free.

Expiry protection uses a per base raw spinlock across queue inspection and a separate expiry lock active only on real time builds and empty otherwise. Interrupt safe callbacks marked TIMER_IRQSAFE drop only the base lock across the call, while other callbacks drop it with interrupts enabled and then wait for concurrent synchronous deleters when waiters are present. A non null running pointer suppresses reentry.

Remote base access requires interrupts disabled and acquires the local base first and then the global base with single depth nesting, releases in reverse order, and asserts both locks held when fetching remote timer events.

The timer softirq run_timer_softirq runs the local base always and, where tickless operation exists, also runs global and default bases and then services remote migration when the tickless timer key is active.

Expiry collection moves the base clock forward to the recorded next expiry, gathers at most one vector per level whose pending bit is set while stopping at the first level whose low clock bits are nonzero and shifting the clock between levels, then advances the clock by one and recomputes next expiry and expires gathered vectors from highest to lowest level while the global tick has reached both clock and next expiry.

Callback invocation copies lockdep state before acquiring it around the call and emits entry and exit traces and warns when no callback is present and detects preemption count imbalance across the call with a one time warning plus restoration of the prior count.

Timer migration is controlled by sysctl timer_migration limited to zero or one and serialized by a dedicated mutex, with writes refreshing a static key enabled only when migration is requested and tickless operation is active. A work item refreshes the same key and enables the tickless timer active key.

Auxiliary clocks appear under a time directory with one numbered child per clock under aux_clocks exposing a readable and writable enable file aux_clock_enable. Decoding uses the first character of the child name masked to three bits. Stores require time administration privilege and valid boolean text, are serialized by a mutex, return early when the requested state matches the active bitmap, and otherwise enable or disable the selected clock and update the bitmap. Creation unwinds children and groups in reverse on failure.

Sleep debugging exposes read only file sleep_time showing nonzero power of two duration bins and service timekeeping_get_mg_floor_swaps summing a per CPU floor swap counter across all possible CPUs with an explicitly racy read.

The sixty four bit jiffy counter jiffies_64 is globally visible and aligned to avoid sharing a cache line, starting from a defined initial value, and this translation unit enables its own trace points.

Auxiliary clock enable changes are serialized by a dedicated mutex using scoped acquisition, and migration key changes plus the sysctl handler plus the key update work are serialized by a separate timer key mutex.
Remote event fetch presets both local and global event times to the maximum value and then delegates to shared next event computation for the addressed CPU bases.
